senātor, senātōris m.

noun, third declension

a senator

A member of the Roman senate, and of the councils of other peoples, the Nervii or the Rhodians (Lewis & Short). Traupman gives it for a modern senator, man or woman; Morgan–Owens for a member of any deliberative body, a town councillor included. Lewis & Short find senātrix, a woman senator, only in Priscian.

Examples

  • mōs anteā senātōribus Rōmae fuit in cūriam cum praetextātīs fīliīs introīre

    it used to be the custom at Rome for senators to bring their young sons with them into the senate houseGell. 1.23.4

See also senate, parliament, council.

SourcesLewis & Short: senator

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. legislator, member of parliament; city councilman.
